title: `argv+=( ... )` throws the positional parameters away and keeps the appended array ACROSS calls — zsh n=4 <1,2,3,X> three times, zshrs n=1 <X>, n=2 <X,X>, n=3 <X,X,X>

observed.notes: Two defects in one line of shell. (a) the append REPLACES the positional parameters instead of extending them, so `$@` is only what was appended; (b) whatever it appends to is not per-frame — the third call sees the two X's the first two left behind, which is why $# climbs 1,2,3 instead of staying 4. `argv=( $argv X )`, `set -- "$@" X` and the same append on a `local -a` array are all pinned as controls and all agree, so the variable is the `+=` form on `argv` specifically, not appends and not argv. Why this is in a COMPLETION evidence base: `Completion/Base/Core/_description` builds its zformat spec list with exactly this append (line 83), so every description compsys renders picks up the leftovers — the upstream Y0*.ztst run in tests/ztst_compsys/ shows it as `DESCRIPTION:{h:file}` where zsh emits `DESCRIPTION:{file}`, and that single misparse accounts for a large share of the failing assertions there.

controls.note: the ASSIGN form of the same append. Agrees (PASS, byte-identical stdout and exit status), which is what makes `+=` the variable
`set --` reaching the same end state. Agrees, so the positional-parameter machinery itself is not broken
`+=` on an ordinary local array. Agrees, so array append is not broken either — only append onto `argv`

variants.note: the shortest witness, and the one the finding was reported as: zsh prints a/b/X, zshrs prints X alone. Observed: 3 line(s) differ — row0 zsh 'a' vs zshrs 'X', row1 zsh 'b' vs '<absent>', row2 zsh 'X' vs '<absent>'
